identity.title: Revealing the complex nature of the strong gravitationally lensed system H-ATLAS J090311.6+003906 using ALMA
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: ALMA Science Verification data on SDP.81 were taken from the ALMA Science Portal [1] (ASP).

evidence.quote: reconstructed the distribution of band 6 and 7 continuum emission in the z = 3.042 source

question.value: What are the physical properties (dust, gas, kinematics, star formation) of the lensed SMG SDP.81, and how does the ALMA-reconstructed submm emission relate to the HST near-IR emission?

evidence.quote: The purpose of this paper is to exploit the high resolution ALMA imaging of the highly magnified lensed source to determine its physical properties.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00016.SV.
using between 22 and 36 12 m-diameter antennas and ALMA's band 4, 6 & 7 receivers.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four 1.875 GHz spectral windows per band, 7.5 GHz total; one or two cover a line, rest continuum

evidence.quote: Four 1.875 GHz bandwidth spectral windows were used, over a total bandwidth of 7.5 GHz.
CO(5-4) (v rest = 576.267 GHz)
CO(8-7) (v rest = 921.799 GHz)
We were unable to detect any significant CO(10-9) emission in the reconstructed band 7 cube.

angular_resolution.value: CO uv-tapered to ~170 mas (1000 kλ); beams 155×121 mas (CO(5-4)), 169×117 mas (CO(8-7))

evidence.quote: 155×121 mas and 169×117 mas for CO(5-4) and CO(8-7), respectively.

sensitivity.value: RMS 0.20 mJy (CO(5-4)) and 0.15 mJy (CO(8-7)) per 21 km/s channel

evidence.quote: The resulting RMS noise levels are 0.20 mJy and 0.15 mJy per 21 kms −1 channel for CO(5-4) and CO(8-7) respectively.
SDP.81 was observed in October 2014 as part of ALMA's Long Baseline Campaign
deeper F160W image which has a total exposure time of 4418 s

what.value: Continuum photometry of the lensed source (table 2 of N14) used in SED fit

evidence.quote: to the fluxes from table 2 in N14 (but de-magnified using our derived continuum source magnification factor)
using the CO(1-0) spectroscopic data acquired by Valtchanov et al. (2011)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Calibration and imaging per ASP scripts, using CASA

evidence.quote: The calibration and imaging of the data is described in the scripts provided on the ASP.

archive_products_used_as_is.value: ASP calibrated data/cubes used; own imaging found ASP data already optimal

evidence.quote: We attempted a variety of different tapers and cleaning parameters but found the ASP data to be already optimal for our purposes.
A robust=1 weighting of the visibilities was used.

uv_taper.value: CO to ~170 mas (1000 kλ); H2O 200 kλ

evidence.quote: were uv-tapered to a resolution of ∼170 mas (1000 kλ)
we binned the band 6 and band 7 continuum images from a pixel scale of 0.005 ′′ to a pixel scale of 0.01 ′′ .
Line-free channels were used to subtract the continuum emission from the CO data.

what.value: Calibration and imaging from ASP scripts / ALMA Partnership paper

evidence.quote: more details can be found in ALMA Partnership, Vlahakis et al. (2015).

what.value: Semi-linear inversion lens modelling with adaptive source grid

evidence.quote: We used the latest implementation of the semi-linear inversion method (Warren & Dye 2003) as described by Nightingale & Dye (2015).
fitted the two dimensional dynamics using an MCMC code (see Swinbank et al. 2012, for further details)

what.value: Dust opacity kappa_850=0.077 m2/kg for consistency

evidence.quote: to be consistent with the fitting in N14

unstated_but_needed: MCMC priors, sampler and chain settings for kinematic fit
Lens model mask definitions and priors/evidence sampler details
Line-free channel ranges and CASA version used by ASP scripts
Two-component SED model functional form and fitting priors

method.value: Image-plane semi-linear inversion with dual reconstruction of band 6 and 7 continuum; power-law elliptical mass plus external shear

evidence.quote: using a dual reconstruction of the ALMA band 6 and band 7 continuum image data
our use of the 2 × 2 pixel binned version of the band 6 and band 7 science verification continuum image data

assumptions.value: Single smooth power-law profile, scale-invariant slope

evidence.quote: we adopted a single smooth powerlaw profile with a volume mass density of the form ρ ∝ r −α

fitting.value: Most probable parameters from marginalising over Bayesian evidence

evidence.quote: most probable lens model parameters identified by marginalising over the Bayesian evidence

validation.value: Image-plane best fit checked in uv plane via MIRIAD uvmodel chi2; offset within uncertainties

evidence.quote: although there is a slight offset in parameter space between the image plane minimum-χ 2 and the uv plane minimum-χ 2, this is within the parameter uncertainties

analysis_steps.goal: Reconstruct CO cubes and moment maps

method.value: Apply best lens model to each channel of CO cubes; moment maps with immoments

evidence.quote: We used our best fit lens model to reconstruct the distribution of flux in the source plane for each slice of the image data cubes
stacking over channels 31 to 61 inclusive

method.value: 2D velocity-field model of Freeman disk plus Burkert halo, MCMC

evidence.quote: we fitted a two dimensional model whose velocity field is described by a combination of stars and gas

key_parameters.value: Dynamical centre within 0.5 kpc of band 7 continuum centroid

evidence.quote: We constrained the [x / y] dynamical centre to be within 0.5 kpc of the band 7 continuum centroid

assumptions.value: Disk rotation; no asymmetric drift correction

evidence.quote: a correction for asymmetric drift need not be applied to the inferred dynamical mass
then fitted the two dimensional dynamics using an MCMC code (see Swinbank et al. 2012, for further details)

validation.value: Residual velocity maps and rotation curves compared

evidence.quote: The best-fit kinematic maps and velocity residuals are shown in Figure 4.

analysis_steps.goal: Dust mass, FIR luminosity, gas mass

method.value: Two-component modified blackbody SED fit to de-magnified fluxes; gas mass via gas-to-dust ratio

evidence.quote: fitting a two-component spectral energy distribution (SED) model to a combination of our measured band 6 and band 7 continuum fluxes
Assuming a typical gas to dust ratio of 150

validation.value: Tested fixed beta=2 and with/without 160 µm flux; dust mass 1.8-2.1e8

evidence.quote: returned a dust mass in the range (1.8 − 2.1) × 10 8 M ⊙

method.value: De-magnify Valtchanov CO(1-0) spectrum using velocity-dependent magnification from CO(5-4) lens reconstruction; alpha_CO=1

evidence.quote: we used the CO luminosity to molecular gas mass conversion factor from Bothwell et al. (2013) of α CO = 1

key_parameters.value: Fixed magnification of 3 at extreme velocities

evidence.quote: we assumed a fixed magnification of 3 in these extremes

used_for.value: Calibration/imaging (ASP scripts) and immoments moment maps

evidence.quote: These were made using CASA immoments

used_for.value: uvmodel to simulate visibilities for uv-plane check

evidence.quote: using MIRIAD uvmodel to produce a simulated visibility dataset

used_for.value: Lens galaxy light removal in HST data

evidence.quote: using the GALFIT software (Peng et al. 2002)
a point spread function created by the TinyTim software package (Krist 1993)
The image was reduced using the IRAF MultiDrizzle package
The best fit disk inclination is (40 ± 5) ◦

Total continuum magnification 15.9 ± 0.7
13.7 ± 0.6 for the CO(5-4) flux and 13.1 ± 0.6 for the CO(8-7) flux

findings_qualitative.value: Dust continuum is clumpy on ~200 pc scales while CO shows smooth disk-like velocity field

evidence.quote: The continuum imaging reveals a highly non-uniform distribution of dust with clumps on scales of ∼ 200 pc.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA disk is offset from the HST near-IR emission

evidence.quote: there is a very distinct offset between the submm emission and the near-IR (rest frame blue) emission

claims.hypothesis: Is the SDP.81 source a rotating disk?
claims.experiment: Fit disk+halo model to reconstructed CO velocity fields
claims.result: Inclination 40±5 deg, v=320 km/s, Mdyn=3.5e10 Msun

evidence.quote: Figure 5 shows the one dimensional rotation curves

claims.experiment: Toomre Q from surface density and dispersion
claims.finding: Disk is collapsing, consistent with merger-induced starburst

evidence.quote: The low value of the Toomre Q parameter and the very irregular distribution of gas are exactly what one would expect if sections of the disk are collapsing to form stars.

claims.hypothesis: Does submm emission align with the near-IR emission?
claims.experiment: Reconstruct ALMA and HST sources with same lens model

evidence.quote: revealed an offset of ∼ 1.5 kpc between the submm and rest-frame optical centroids

why_this_method.value: Image-plane modelling is more sensitive for the figure of merit and far more efficient than uv-plane

evidence.quote: modelling in the image plane is vastly more efficient than working directly with the extremely large visibility dataset

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pure SIE model fit the ring but had lower evidence

evidence.quote: the model has a lower evidence (with ∆χ 2 ≃ 20) than the most probable model

limitations_admitted.value: Differential magnification neglected; large uncertainties in gas conversion factors

evidence.quote: we have of course neglected any effects of differential magnification
image pixels are correlated by the beam which biases image plane modelling

referee_caveats_inferred: Image-plane fit ignores pixel covariance so evidences are not strictly comparable
Gas masses depend strongly on assumed gas-to-dust ratio and alpha_CO
Dynamical mass assumes disk geometry from a lensed, tapered cube
